architecture.mechanism: Pilots' attention allocation and workload are monitored via eye-tracking metrics (fixation duration, fixation number, pupil diameter) and weighted via inter-criteria correlation (CRITIC) method to detect and adapt to high-workload critical phases such as autorotative glide after engine failure.
architecture.intervention: Add a driver-state monitor to the engine management system that uses a driver-facing camera with eye-tracking (fixation duration, blink rate, pupil diameter) and an attention/workload index computed by the CRITIC method across multiple eye-movement metrics; when the index indicates a sudden high-workload or distraction event coincident with a pending misfire/stall fault, the ECU pre-emptively holds fuel injection and ignition in a fail-safe mode, illuminates the check-engine/MIL lamp and stores the DTC so OBD diagnostics remain intact, rather than abruptly cutting power.
architecture.expected_effect: Reduces sudden, unintended engine stalls and intermittent power loss by preventing hazardous fuel-cut events during transient high-workload/distraction conditions, while preserving OBD-II check-engine reporting and safe vehicle operation.
architecture.falsification_test: On a 2020 Hyundai Elantara fleet, instrument 20 vehicles with the eye-tracking + CRITIC workload module and 20 controls; drive over a standardized mixed-condition route (highway cruise, sudden throttle lift, transient misfire injection) and count (a) sudden-stall and power-loss events per 1,000 km, and (b) OBD MIL/DTC capture rate for induced faults. The intervention is falsified if the equipped group's stall/power-loss rate is not statistically lower (p<0.05) than controls, or if MIL/DTC capture rate drops below 99% of the control rate.
